# Joint Schur funding and an equal-central-pair exclusion

This note concerns the remaining tetrahedral stochastic-capacity configuration with two full rows x,y and one one-zero row z. It proves an exact joint curvature test, and proves that test strictly when the other two central centroid coordinates agree. It does not settle the unequal-coordinate case or OC.

The common actual section centroid is b, with a unique noncentral coordinate b_h>1/3. The zero row has hole h. By `candidate 8bce978d82ec174e`, both full-row cuts are strict quadrilaterals: x captures {h,j}, y captures the complementary pair {l,m}. Their raw margins satisfy the exact column balance there.

Normalize the positive objective weights so that the common multiplier sum is 1. Then the weighted full-row gradient is b. If P_i is a full row's cap fraction, its objective weight is P_i^(1/3). Write

    c_i=t_i 1-X_i,       f_i=f_(sum c_ij E_j)(0)=P_i/t_i,
    z_h=0, z_j=w/b_j (j!=h), w>0.

Let H_i be the Hessian of the cap probability with respect to the ACTUAL raw margins c_i. No threshold-normalized Hessian is substituted for it below.

## 1. Exact joint funding of the corrected pair directions

Put v=b_m e_l-b_l e_m, so b dot v=0 and v_h=0. The cap x excludes this central pair, while cap y captures it. Applying the audited central-pair cap theorem to the complement of x and to y gives

    v^T H_x v>0,        v^T H_y v<0.

For each full row let kappa_i be the explicit constant that corrects v by kappa_i 1 in the Schur formula. In actual raw units it is

    kappa_i=t_i^2 (1^T H_i v)/(3P_i).

The all-dimensional Schur identity, including the scale of the row, gives

    weight_i (v+kappa_i1)^T Hess(phi_3)(X_i)(v+kappa_i1)
         =-v^T H_i v/(3 f_i).                        (1)

Define the strictly positive numbers

    A=(v^T H_x v)/(3f_x),
    B=-(v^T H_y v)/(3f_y),
    C=2 b_l^2 b_m^2/w.                               (2)

For arbitrary real alpha,beta, put K=alpha kappa_x+beta kappa_y and use the row motions

    delta x=alpha(v+kappa_x1)-Kx,
    delta y=beta(v+kappa_y1)-Ky,
    delta z=-(alpha+beta)v-Kz.                        (3)

Their sum is zero exactly, because x+y+z=1. The zero row retains its zero at h. All positive entries stay positive in both signs for a sufficiently small parameter. These are therefore actual feasible stochastic variations, not formal row variations lacking funding.

Homogeneity makes every radial Hessian term and radial cross term vanish. The weighted geometric-mean Hessian of the zero row, on its three positive coordinates, is

    (1/w)[bb^T/3-diag(b_j^2)].                       (4)

Here b in (4) is restricted to j!=h. Since the indicated pair vector has weighted sum zero, its value is -C. Combining (1)–(4), the full weighted second variation is exactly

    -A alpha^2+B beta^2-C(alpha+beta)^2.              (5)

For fixed beta, its maximum over alpha is

    [B-AC/(A+C)] beta^2,

attained at alpha=-C beta/(A+C). Consequently

    B>AC/(A+C)                                      (6)

excludes a local maximum. Equivalently 1/B<1/A+1/C. The zero-row curvature has been retained, and the correction constants need not be equal.

## 2. Equal central coordinates force two equal heights in each plane

Now assume b_l=b_m=b0. The archived diagonal-centroid calculation in `candidate 7fd42b1082a20d4b`, Section 4, uses ONLY equality and centrality of these two coordinates to force their raw heights equal. Its proof is included briefly here. Normalize the reciprocal diagonal coordinates as (a,b,c,d) with sum 1, and put r=ab,s=cd. Then

    3(b_l-b_m)=(c-d)[r-(r-s)^2]/D,

where D=(a+c)(a+d)(b+c)(b+d)>0. Centrality implies (s-r)c<=r and (s-r)d<=r. If r>=s, then (r-s)^2<r. If s>r and (s-r)^2>=r, the larger of c,d is at least sqrt(s), contradicting those two inequalities. Thus the bracket is strictly positive and c=d. The equal raw heights follow by reciprocal normalization.

Orient both planes toward {h,j}; the second orientation is the complement of the actual y cap. Scale each to have margins

    (p,q,-1,-1),       p,q>0,

in the order h,j,l,m. Set U=1/(1+p), V=1/(1+q), and T=2-U-V. Exact section integration gives

    3 b_h=U(1+T-U)/T,
    3 b_j=V(1+T-V)/T,
    P=1-UV(3-U-V),
    f=UVT.                                          (7)

Because b_h>1/3 and b_j<=1/3, the first two formulas imply U>T and V<=T, respectively. Since 0<U,V<1, this forces

    1/2<T<1.                                        (8)

Let the two values be T_X,T_Q, where Q denotes the plane oppositely oriented to y. Write a0=b_h, c0=b_j, so a0+c0+2b0=1. Eliminating U,V from (7) gives

    UV=T^2-(1+3b0)T+1,
    U-V=3(a0-c0)T/(2T-1),
    (4b0-T)(2T-1)^2=3(a0-c0)^2T.                    (9)

The planes are distinct. Otherwise their actual margins would be proportional with opposite orientations, and their sum could not have negative h coordinate but nonnegative j coordinate as required by the column balance. Since the centroid and T determine U-V in (9), T_X!=T_Q.

For the unscaled plane (p,q,-1,-1), direct differentiation in the antisymmetric negative pair e_l-e_m gives

    (e_l-e_m)^T H_P(e_l-e_m)/(3f)
      =J(T):=2b0-4b0T+(2/3)T^2>0.                  (10)

For an explicit verification before using (9), the numerator divided by 3f is

    2[(U+V-1)^3+UV(3-2U-2V)]/[3(2-U-V)].

Substitution of (9) gives (10). Positivity also follows independently from the central-pair cap theorem applied to the complementary cap.

## 3. The actual column coefficients and the exact positive gap

Write the actual margins as alpha0(p_X,q_X,-1,-1) for x and -beta0(p_Q,q_Q,-1,-1) for y, where alpha0,beta0>0. The column equations yield

    beta0-alpha0=w(1/b0-3),
    alpha0 q_X-beta0 q_Q=w(1/c0-3).                  (11)

In particular q_X!=q_Q. Put R=alpha0/w. Then

    R=[1/c0-3+(1/b0-3)q_Q]/(q_X-q_Q),
    beta0/w=R+1/b0-3.                               (12)

For the pair e_l-e_m, instead of its harmless multiple b0(e_l-e_m), the constants in (2) become

    A=J(T_X)/alpha0, B=J(T_Q)/beta0, C=2b0^2/w.

Thus (6) is equivalent to positivity of the exact reciprocal gap

    E=1/(2b0^2)-[(R+1/b0-3)/J(T_Q)-R/J(T_X)].        (13)

We prove E>0. Set

    u=2T_X-1, v=2T_Q-1, zeta=sqrt(3(u+v+uv)).

By (8), 0<u,v<1 and 0<zeta<3. Factoring the cubic equation in (9) using its two distinct roots gives

    b0=T_X T_Q(T_X+T_Q-1)/(4T_XT_Q-1),
    a0-c0=(2T_X-1)(2T_Q-1)/sqrt(3(4T_XT_Q-1)).       (14)

The positive sign in the second identity is fixed by a0>c0. Equivalently

    v=(zeta^2/3-u)/(1+u),
    b0=(3u^2+zeta^2)(zeta^2+3)/[24zeta^2(1+u)].      (15)

Substitute (12), (14)–(15) into (13), using (7) to express q=1/V-1. Clearing and refactoring gives the exact identity

    E= -(3u+zeta)^2
           [3u^2-2u zeta+zeta^2-2zeta]
           [u zeta-3u+zeta^2+zeta]^2
        /[36zeta(1+u)(3u^2+zeta^2)^2
                         J(T_X)J(T_Q)].              (16)

All denominators are positive. The second squared factor is nonzero: v>0 gives u<zeta^2/3, and zeta<3, so

    u zeta-3u+zeta^2+zeta
       > -(zeta^2/3)(3-zeta)+zeta^2+zeta
       =zeta+zeta^3/3>0.                             (17)

The remaining bracket is strictly negative. For fixed 0<u<1 it is a convex quadratic in zeta. The condition 0<v<1 places zeta strictly between sqrt(3u) and sqrt(3+6u). At the first endpoint its value is

    (u+1)sqrt(3u)[sqrt(3u)-2]<0.

At the second endpoint its value is

    (u+1)[3(u+1)-2sqrt(3+6u)]<0,

because 9(u+1)^2-4(3+6u)=3(3u+1)(u-1)<0. Convexity bounds every intermediate value by the larger of these two negative endpoint values. Equations (16)–(17) therefore prove E>0.

The feasible motion (3), with the maximizing choice following (5), now has strictly positive weighted second variation. This contradicts local maximality. Hence the remaining two-full/one-zero tetrahedral maximum cannot have b_l=b_m. Equality b_j=1/3 is included: no strict bound on that coordinate was used.

The unequal b_l,b_m case still requires a genuine comparison of the two actual cap stiffnesses. Formula (6) is not asserted automatically there.


## Subsequent removal of the equal-central-pair assumption in this stratum

The source `candidate 558c9d47421b8323` proves from the actual positive vertex-hole pencil that the two excluded central centroid coordinates necessarily agree. Combined with the present strict funding inequality and the complementary-quad incidence theorem, this excludes the full two-full/one-one-zero-row tetrahedral stratum, not just an assumed symmetry subfamily. The separate three-full-row case is not covered by that inference.
